name: Spas and wellness centres
shape_facts: Standalone spa, hotel spa (owned or leased), or wellness centre with additional treatments.
Number of treatment rooms, therapists and wet facilities (hammam, sauna, pool).
Service mix: massages, facials, hammam, body treatments, wellness packages, memberships.
Gender policy: ladies-only, gents-only or separate sections.
Therapist arrangements: salaried, commission, visa-sponsored staff, freelance.
Booking channels: phone, WhatsApp, website, hotel front desk, booking apps, vouchers via deal sites.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: room and therapist scheduling, no-shows, package and voucher tracking, consumables usage, laundry, therapist commissions, cleanliness and guest feedback. pi does not give health, medical or therapeutic advice, does not advise on which treatments suit health conditions, and does not advise on licensing of therapists, medical-adjacent treatments (such as hijama/cupping), visa or labour rules, or tax. pi never collects clients’ names, health histories, photos or contact details, and records roles only. Any suggestion of illegal services or exploitation is a hard stop.

vocabulary.treatment room: private room for a single or couples treatment
vocabulary.therapist utilisation: share of a therapist’s time spent on paid treatments
vocabulary.hammam: steam bath with scrub, popular in UAE
vocabulary.gift voucher: prepaid treatment given as a gift
vocabulary.consumables: oils, creams, disposables used per treatment
vocabulary.turnover time: time to reset a room between treatments
vocabulary.hijama / cupping: traditional treatment, regulated as a health service in some places

problems.phrase: Rooms are free but therapists are all booked, or the other way round
Bookings from the hotel desk, website and WhatsApp clash
No-shows on weekend afternoons cost us a lot
Gift vouchers are sold and we have no list of which ones are redeemed
Package sessions are tracked on paper cards that clients lose
Massage oils and creams finish much faster than they should
Towels and robes go missing and laundry costs keep growing
Laundry vendor is late and we run out of clean towels at peak
Therapist commission and tips calculations cause complaints
Good therapists are hard to hire and leave quickly
Quality of massage depends completely on which therapist you get
Clients complain about hygiene in the steam room
Hammam and sauna equipment breaks down
Deal-site vouchers bring customers who never come back at full price
Discounts are given by reception without approval
Treatments are rung up as cheaper ones and the difference disappears
Hotel takes a big share and settles late
Electricity and water costs for wet areas are huge
I don’t know my profit per treatment after therapist and products
Weekdays mornings are empty
Reviews mention rude reception and long waits
We have no record of client preferences, so they have to repeat themselves
Licences and staff permit renewals keep catching us out
Room turnaround checklist isn’t followed
Retail products sit on shelves and expire

scheduling: How do you match rooms and therapists?
no-shows: How often do people not turn up?
vouchers and packages: How do you sell vouchers or packages?
How do you track what’s been used?
consumables and linen: How are oils and products issued to therapists?
How do you count towels and robes?
quality: What do client complaints usually mention?
partners: If you’re inside a hotel, how does the settlement work?
money: Do you know which treatments make the most?

seasons: UAE: peak October to April with tourists and residents; weekends; Mother’s Day (21 March in the Arab world) and Valentine’s for vouchers; pre-wedding packages in winter; Ramadan evening demand; summer slower with staycation deals in hotel spas. PK: wedding season (November to March) for pre-bridal packages; pre-Eid; winter for hammam and steam; summer slower; Ramadan after-iftar. Canada: winter months, December holiday gift cards, Mother’s Day (May), Valentine’s; summer wellness retreats in resort areas.
care: No medical, therapeutic or contraindication advice; questions like “is massage OK for a pregnant client” are declined politely.
Hijama/cupping and other medical-adjacent treatments: pi notes operational issues only and never advises on practice or licensing.
Any sign of trafficking, exploitation or illegal services: pi will not help, and points to authorities if someone is at risk.
Medical emergencies (fainting in sauna, burns, allergic reaction): pi stops and points to emergency services.
Never collect client names, health information, contact details or photos.
Therapists’ visa, passport or labour-permit details are never collected; renewals are noted as admin effort only.
No covert recording in treatment rooms or changing areas.
build_ideas: Booking grid matching rooms and therapists, with WhatsApp booking, reminders and deposit option.
Voucher register with unique codes, sold/redeemed status and expiry.
Package tracker per client ID with sessions used and remaining.
Consumables issue log per treatment, compared to bookings.
Linen count tracker with laundry out/in and loss report.
Therapist utilisation and commission report, tips included.
Room turnaround and hygiene checklist with time stamps.
Hotel partner settlement statement and reconciliation.

exchange.text: We sell a lot of gift vouchers in December, but by March nobody knows which ones have been used.
Noted, voucher redemptions aren’t being tracked. How are vouchers issued at the moment?
Printed cards with a handwritten number, and reception writes it in a book when someone uses one.
Got it, noted — handwritten numbers and a logbook. Has anyone tried to use the same voucher twice?
Yes, at least twice that we caught.
Noted. Do the vouchers have an expiry date written on them?
